item.text: Card text: "Have you checked visa requirements?"

why: Bullet 2 ("a topic the student's own facts make irrelevant is suppressed") never uses the word 'approved', while bullet 3 explicitly says 'AN APPROVED FACT is never asked again'. It is unclear whether topic-level suppression requires the underlying destination fact to be counsellor-approved, or whether any extracted (needs-review) fact is enough to pre-emptively hide a whole topic.
open_question: Does bullet 2's topic-suppression require the grounding fact to be counsellor-APPROVED (matching bullet 3's explicit qualifier and B3's approval gate), or does an unapproved, needs-review extraction suffice on its own? If a pending, later-rejected 'India-only' reading pre-emptively hides all visa content before the counsellor confirms it, an application draft could miss a needed visa step -- the contract does not say which way to fail safe here.

facts.value: engineering (approved 8 months ago, before a school change)

item.text: Card text: "What are you hoping to study?"

why: Bullet 3 says an approved fact is never asked again, with no stated expiry. D-013's validFrom/validTo model exists in ARCHITECTURE for fact history, but B18 gives no rule for when (if ever) enough time or context change makes a re-ask legitimate.
open_question: Does an approved fact stay permanently un-askable, or is there an implicit staleness window (tied to validFrom/validTo, session boundaries, or elapsed time) after which the counsellor may legitimately re-confirm it? The contract states no expiry condition or re-confirmation trigger.

item.text: Card text: "Would scholarship options be worth exploring?"

why: F7 assumes do-not-ask entries are sometimes key-level (family_income does not cover a distinct scholarship-eligibility key, F7-02) and sometimes topic-level (visa_topic covers all visa cards regardless of country, F7-03). The contract gives no data model, matching rule, or worked example that distinguishes the two.
open_question: Is a do-not-ask entry always scoped to one exact fact key, always a broader topic/category, or does the counsellor/student choose the granularity per entry? Without a stated matching rule, an implementation could reasonably go either narrower or broader than intended on every entry.

item.text: Card text (student said in a LATER turn, "actually, you can ask about that now"): "What is your family's annual income?"

why: Bullet 4 only states that a listed item is never raised; it says nothing about whether the list can be edited or revoked, by whom, or how a revocation is recorded. B15's erasure flow has an explicit confirm/audit machinery; B18's do-not-ask list has no analogous mechanism described.
open_question: Can a student (or counsellor, on the student's behalf) revoke a do-not-ask entry mid-session or in a later session? If so, what confirms the revocation and where is it recorded? The contract is silent on the list's mutability entirely.

facts.value: the student states an abroad destination in the SAME turn the scribe is producing this output

item.text: Visa fact slot generated as part of the same processing step that also just recorded the destination update.

why: B18's proof language ("an India-only student produces zero visa items") describes an outcome without naming an evaluation-timing boundary. It is unclear whether an item generated in the very same turn/processing step as a fact-changing utterance should reflect the old or the new fact state.
open_question: When a destination-changing fact and an item's generation happen within the same turn or processing step, does suppression apply based on the fact state before or after that turn's update lands? The contract's outcome-only phrasing does not specify a snapshot boundary.

item.text: Card text: "Do you need an entry permit for your program?" (paraphrased, never uses the word 'visa')

why: Bullet 2 gives exactly one worked example (visa items for an India-only student) and names no topic taxonomy, category enumeration, or matching mechanism. It is unclear whether 'topic' matching is by a fixed enumerated category mapped from facts to items, or by literal keyword/lexical overlap between the fact and the item text.
open_question: Is a 'topic' for bullet-2 purposes matched via a fixed, contract- (or code-) defined category list (e.g. visa, financial-aid, exam-prep, ...), or via free-text/keyword similarity between the destination fact and the item's wording? A paraphrase that avoids the literal word 'visa' (e.g. 'entry permit') would be handled very differently under each reading, and the contract does not say which is intended.

facts.value: "maybe I'll take a gap year and then decide if I want to go abroad"

item.text: Card text: "Here is a general overview of student visa options, for when you're ready."

why: The contract's suppression model is binary (suppress vs surface). A gap-year-then-maybe-abroad fact is neither a settled India-only fact nor a settled abroad destination -- it sits between the two headline cases with no stated treatment.
open_question: Does an explicitly undecided, deferred-intent fact like this leave the visa topic simply un-suppressed (nothing has made it irrelevant yet), or does the contract intend some softer treatment (e.g. lower-priority evidence-only content, no direct questions) for genuinely uncertain destination signals? B18 has no concept of partial relevance, only a binary suppress/surface outcome.

facts.status: approved (recorded in an earlier counselling session, months before the current one)

item.text: Card text, in a NEW session: "Can you confirm your IELTS score?"

why: B18's own worked example ("a student with a known fact gets no card or question asking for that fact") is framed within a session's scribe output, but ARCHITECTURE H3 describes a longitudinal, cross-session Student Knowledge Graph. It is unclear whether 'already known' for bullet 3 means known anywhere in that longitudinal graph, or only within the current session's approved facts.
open_question: Does bullet 3's 'never asked again' apply across the student's entire longitudinal history (any prior session), or is 'already known' scoped to the current session only? If longitudinal, does staleness (b18-u-02) or a counsellor override ever reopen it?

item.text: Comparison card: "IELTS vs TOEFL -- here's how the prep timelines compare, in case you want to switch."

why: Bullet 3's literal text restricts 'a card or question asking for that fact'. A comparison card does not literally ask a question, but it can functionally reopen an already-decided choice (which exam to take) by inviting reconsideration. B1 defines card TYPES (question/comparison/evidence) but B18 does not say how comparison or evidence cards relate to a fact that is already decided, only to the literal act of asking.
open_question: Does bullet 3's protection against re-asking extend to a comparison card that implicitly invites reconsidering an already-approved, already-decided choice, or does it apply only to the literal question-type re-ask (as F9-03's non-reopening comparison example assumes)? The contract does not distinguish 'informative comparison using a known value' from 'comparison that invites revisiting a settled decision'.

facts.value: the student's parent, not the student, said "please don't bring up our finances" in a joint session

item.text: Card text: "What is your family's annual income?"

why: D-026 ties the auto-verify property specifically to the STUDENT being the turn's speaker (B2). B18's text says only "the student's own facts" and "the student's do-not-ask list", without addressing a joint session where a parent or guardian voices a fact or an instruction on the student's behalf.
open_question: Does a do-not-ask instruction or a fact voiced by a parent/guardian in a joint counselling session carry the same weight under B18 as one voiced by the student directly? The contract's 'student's own facts' / 'student's do-not-ask list' wording does not address multi-speaker sessions at all.

facts.value: withdrawn (approved AFTER a Canada visa card was already shown and left on screen)

item.text: The Canada visa card shown earlier in the same session, still displayed after the withdrawal fact landed.

why: F2-05 assumes suppression is evaluated fresh at each new item-generation moment, so a withdrawal fact simply stops NEW Canada-visa items from being produced. B18's proof language ("the scribe suppresses", "produces zero visa items") describes what the scribe currently produces, not whether an item already shown before the underlying fact changed must be retracted or hidden retroactively.
open_question: When a fact that justified showing an item later changes (e.g. a withdrawn application), must an already-displayed card/item be retracted or hidden, or does B18 only govern what gets produced going forward? The contract's outcome language is about production, not retroactive retraction of prior output.
